pairs.reason: Which option governs: plan-01 records that O4 governs; plan-04 records what O4's truthfulness contract keeps in place of a configured value.
Which option governs: the plan and the spec each record that O4 governs and that O1 is telemetry completion.
Which option governs: the spec records that O4 governs; plan-04 records what O4's truthfulness contract requires.
Is O2 adopted: the plan and the spec each reject the proxy as architecturally insufficient, since it cannot see the gateway's later hop.
Is O3 relied on: the plan and the spec each keep it opportunistic, since no standard signal exists and nothing depends on it.
Is the filter applied on the reconcile path: both pages record the one decision that it is wired to both paths, plan-08 finishing plan-07's reversal.
Execution authority over production routing: E3 and E1 each decide for their own increment that it holds none.
Execution authority over production routing: E3's guard and increment A's inertness proof, each for its own increment.
Execution authority over production routing: E3 extends E2's standing authority-guard test to its own modules.
Execution authority over production routing: E3 holds none by extending E2's guard, which E2 records as adding no runtime authority.
Execution authority over production routing: E1 adds none and increment A edits no driver path, each for its own increment.
Execution authority over production routing: E2's guard extends E1's diff guard to its own branch.
Execution authority over production routing: E2 adds none and proves it the same way E1 did, in nearly E1's words.
Execution authority over production routing: increment A's inertness proof and E2's guard, each for its own increment.
Execution authority over production routing: increment A's inertness proof and E2's no-authority rule, each for its own increment.
Execution authority over production routing: two decisions of the one E2 plan each record that E2 holds none, proven by the diff guard.
Where redaction is applied: E1 scrubs at the writer; E2 renders E1's scrubbed artifacts verbatim and proves the chain.
Where the evidence consumer lives: E3 and E2 each place their own module in session analytics, read-only over E1.
How the Studio surface is built and verified: E3's calibration panel and E2's routing tab, each verified in a browser for its own increment.
What E1's evidence sets gain: plan-01 names the two labelled additions as decision 11; plan-11 specifies them.
When a report is current: plan-03 binds reports to corpus and policy; plan-02's gates G3 and G5 require that binding.
How missing evidence is carried: plan-04 propagates an unavailable measure as insufficient evidence; plan-09 carries an arm that cannot run the same way.
When a router score may be reported: plan-06 requires the complete control set; plan-09 says an insufficient arm never satisfies it.
How an unreported cost is recorded: E1's run record and increment G's usage block each state it explicitly, never as zero, for their own record.
How an unreported cost is recorded: E1's unavailable provenance and increment G's unavailable basis, each for its own record.
How an unreported cost is recorded: plan-02 sets the four states; plan-05 fixes what unavailable means and that 0.00 is never written.
How a new field stays compatible: increment G's usage block follows increment F, additive and optional so older documents keep loading.
What a failure class means and does: increment A classifies cause only and leaves the action to B; B's table maps each class to its action.
Whether a requested model stands in for the effective one: A's result never sets them equal; B's launch keeps the never-assumed rule as a tri-state.
What the state store holds: D extends B's store under the same schema with probe states and keeps B's decay to unknown.
How an auth-disabled profile returns: B leaves it to the operator; D's enable command moves it to probe_due, never straight to eligible.
Whether the numbers are configuration: E3's thresholds are configuration, D's backoff numbers are named defaults, each for its own numbers.
Whether the numbers are configuration: E3's thresholds are configuration, B's cooldowns are named defaults, each for its own numbers.
Whether the numbers are configuration: E3's thresholds are configuration, C's repair limits are named defaults, each for its own numbers.
Whether the numbers are configuration: D's backoff and B's cooldowns are each named defaults, journaled, not configuration.
Whether the numbers are configuration: D's backoff and C's repair limits are each named defaults, journaled, not configuration.
Whether the numbers are configuration: B's cooldowns and C's repair limits are each named defaults, journaled, not configuration.
Whether the repository block may widen policy: D's routing.recovery object applies increment A's restriction-only rule.
Which commands stay pure: D keeps A's validate, status and explain pure and adds tick and enable as the commands that write.
Which commands stay pure: C's task-addressed explain extends A's explain and stays pure configuration resolution.
Which commands stay pure: D's tick and C's task-addressed explain each extend A's commands for their own increment, explain staying pure.
What scope binds the reconciler: plan-05's cumulative allowlist binds the reconciler too; plan-09 applies it to reconciliation.
When independence cannot be established: B's flows keep their non-blocking disposition; C's reconciliation fails closed with its own.
What the routing-run record carries: plan-04 adds the telemetry fields per attempt; plan-07 defines the versioned schema around them.
Whether a requirement rides in the packet: F reads the context requirement beside the packet because C's envelope is frozen and digest-bound.
Whether a Tier-2 profile may be selected: C's route classes unlock it under its legality rules; with no route class B's filter stands.
How a member's identity is established: plan-03 takes a declared identity, attribution not authentication; plan-08 leaves authentication to the epic.
Which lock serialises ledger mutations: the worktree plan's repo-scoped lock, which the team controller extracts and shares by lock name.
Which scopes may loosen security: the env scrub's opt-out is honoured only from trusted scopes, under the harness's monotonic security floor.
Which scopes may loosen security: the scrub's tighten-only in-repo layers apply the harness's monotonic security floor to one setting.
Which scopes may loosen security: plan-01 defers which scopes may opt out of the scrub to decision 5, which plan-05 records.
What init ignores: spec-02 keeps .cct/ ignored and needs no exception; spec-05 adds the personal override file beside it.
How a project moves its configuration: an explicit command only, and the fallback window during which the old location is still read.
How a project moves its configuration: spec-05 names the explicit command spec-03 requires.
How a project moves its configuration: the migrate command of spec-05 and the fallback window of spec-04 serve the same move.
Where project configuration lives: the later ruling puts it in .cct.toml at the repository root, replacing the earlier trusted project files as its location.
Where project configuration lives: spec-05 places the personal override and the manifest, which the harness plan does not name.
Where project configuration lives: spec-05 puts the companion files beside spec-01's .cct.toml at the repository root.
Which requests must pass the Origin check: every non-GET method, by method not by route list (plan-04); a request with no Origin header passes, for non-browser clients (plan-02).
Whether a rejection echoes the offending text: neither does, each for its own response: the guard's 403 is a constant message, the probe never returns the matched exception text.
Which SQLite DSNs the probe accepts: a file DSN whose file is missing is rejected, not created (plan-03); the in-memory form, touching no path, is accepted (plan-04).

How the error response names the failure class: the DSN plan adds three codes to the closed code set rather than folding them into bad_dsn, building on the error_code field the error-hardening plan adds beside error.
Whether the studio changes: the DSN plan confirms the settings page renders any string; the error-hardening plan keeps error so no UI change is needed; each for its own slice.
Whether the studio changes: the settings page renders any string (DSN plan) and the studio stays untouched since it renders the curated message (error-hardening plan), each for its own slice.
Whether the studio changes: plan-03 leaves the studio untouched because plan-01 keeps error beside the new error_code; plan-01's decision is the response field, plan-03 applies it to the studio.
Whether the response changes for its consumers: the error response keeps error and only adds error_code (plan-01); the success response is unchanged (plan-04); each for its own response.

Whether a capture of the installed CLI settles the launch integration: Codex's -c overrides are adopted only once the capture proves nested keys; Pi's overlay form waits for slice D's capture; each for its own harness.

Whether a capture of the installed CLI settles the launch integration: Codex's overlay form is adopted only after its capture; Kiro's model ids, resume and headless details come from slice E's capture; each for its own harness.
Whether a capture of the installed CLI settles the launch integration: Pi's overlay form is ruled at slice D's capture, Kiro's launch details at slice E's; each for its own harness.

What the catalog reuses from routing's scripts: routing-config.sh's line lexer, extracted into a shared library (spec-04); routing-probe.sh's canary primitives and tri-state, not its accounting (spec-06); each for its own component.
What may count as evidence that a binding is supported: an unverified launch never records supported (spec-07); an endpoint's quirk declaration is never evidence (spec-08); each for its own case.
Which artifact CCT runs: the launcher runs only the venv's exact 0.9.0 (plan-03), enforcing at run time the hashed-wheel pin of plan-01; it builds on the pin.
Which artifact CCT runs: CI installs the exact wheel plan-01 pins, so it tests what production runs (plan-11); it applies the pin to CI.
How upstream may change what CCT runs: only by a CCT commit; plan-01 pins the artifact for that reason, plan-13 makes each pin bump a reviewed atomic CCT change; the bump procedure builds on the pin.

What a missing or mismatched prerequisite does: setup warns with the cause and remedy and exits 0 unless the wiki was requested (plan-02); the launcher stops before side effects and names the setup command (plan-03); each for its own step.

What a missing prerequisite does: checkout setup installs the lock or warns (plan-02); plugin-only and copied-adapter guidance names the external prerequisite and refuses lint rather than skip it (plan-04); each for its own installation mode.

What a missing or mismatched prerequisite does: setup warns and reports a distinct incomplete result (plan-02); doctor gives a missing venv, a missing distribution and a version mismatch separate outcomes and remedies (plan-10); each for its own command.

Which Python versions the wiki needs: setup keeps non-wiki CCT usable on a 3.10-only or 3.14-only host with the wiki unavailable (plan-02); CI tests the wiki on 3.11–3.13 without dropping 3.10 for other features and names setup as where that shows (plan-11); it builds on setup's distinction.

What a missing or mismatched prerequisite does: the managed launcher stops before side effects (plan-03); unmanaged guidance verifies the version before lint and refuses (plan-04); each for its own installation mode.

What doctor checks to call the tooling healthy: plan-03 shares the launcher's resolver with doctor so healthy means the bytes the next command runs; plan-10 names D3's resolver and builds its report on it.
Which artifact CCT runs: wiki-lint CI is retargeted to the same artifact and launcher plan-03 defines (plan-11); it applies the launcher to CI.
What a missing or mismatched prerequisite does: unmanaged guidance refuses lint (plan-04); doctor reports each failure with its own outcome and remedy (plan-10); each for its own surface.

Which installations CCT claims to set up: plan-04 limits managed setup to checkouts and names the external prerequisite for the rest; the catalogue and docs state that same reach (plan-12); it applies plan-04's boundary to the documents.

How the duplicate engines are retired: plan-05 deletes both and retargets every caller; plan-14 makes that deletion the last green stage, after the launcher, package and CI replacement; it sequences plan-05's deletion.

Whether the legacy manifest-less mode is kept: plan-06's rewritten test proves the verbs and audit-flush in manifest-less mode; plan-08 keeps the wiki manifest-less on the strength of that round trip; it builds on plan-06's proof.
What the contract test runs against: plan-06 rewrites it around the exact package launcher; CI runs that thin contract on the exact wheel (plan-11); it applies plan-06's test to CI.

How the schema's divergence is checked: plan-07 pins the reconciled project fingerprint in the thin contract; doctor reports the schema source and fingerprint and gives drift its own outcome (plan-10); it checks plan-07's pin.
How the schema's divergence is kept current: a pin bump updates plan-07's classification, delta and fingerprint atomically (plan-13); the bump procedure builds on plan-07's record.

Whether the swap takes on governance: plan-08 runs no init and adds no manifest, approvals or findings; the documents keep governance explicitly out of scope (plan-12); it states plan-08's boundary in the docs.
How the schema's divergence is kept current: a pin bump updates the fingerprint and the doctor statements plan-10 reports (plan-13); the bump procedure builds on the doctor report.

Whether flushing is tied to another command: a verb, not a flag on ingest, so no coupling to an ingest run (flush spec-01); independent of promote, with no hook or auto-invoke (flush spec-05); each for its own neighbour.

When flush refuses: a log whose committed blob is not a byte prefix of the working file is refused (flush spec-02); a detached HEAD or an unrelated dirty tree is not (flush spec-06); each for its own state.
When flush refuses: flush spec-07 adds the v1 validation to the pending detection flush spec-02 defines, with the same refusal and the same rule that the ledger is never edited.
When flush refuses: unrelated dirty state is tolerated (flush spec-06); a torn or invalid line in the log itself is refused (flush spec-07); each for its own state.
What the pathspec commit captures: only the ingest log's working state (flush spec-03), so flush spec-06 tolerates a detached HEAD and other changes by construction.
What the pathspec commit captures: the whole file's bytes, as flush spec-03 commits it, so flush spec-07 refuses a malformed log rather than persist it.
How the working log is checked: trail spec-03 makes it append-only NDJSON after a fixed marker line; flush spec-02 builds on that to count pending lines after the committed prefix.
How the working log is checked: flush spec-07 runs the v1 format validation trail spec-03 gives wiki lint over the working log before counting or committing.
What the archive holds: trail spec-01 lays out the directory with plan.json and proposal.md; trail spec-02 adds curator-delta.md to it only when the curator edited the proposal.
How the archive is written: trail spec-05 makes it atomic with the wiki write because trail spec-01 places .audit/ under knowledge/wiki/.
How the archive is written: the curator delta trail spec-02 writes at promote is part of the archive trail spec-05 stages into promote's temporary tree.
How a log line names its archive: trail spec-01 names the archive by the proposal directory's name, reused verbatim; trail spec-09 records that basename as proposal_dir.
What the record carries: trail spec-08 moves the append after materialization so the proposal_hash trail spec-03 defines hashes the written proposal directory.
What the record carries: trail spec-03 fixes the format, source and hash fields; trail spec-09 adds the patch-set fields (derived disposition, proposal_dir, target_paths, page_types).
What the record carries: trail spec-08's build_log_record derives the one record shape trail spec-09 defines from a WikiPatchSet or an IngestProposal.
Whether lines are cross-checked against archives: trail spec-03 defers the semantic checks; trail spec-04 names an accept line with no matching archive as the hook point for that deferred pass.
Which runs write a line: trail spec-05 keeps the append out of promote's atomic unit because it must record the rejects trail spec-04 puts in scope.

Which runs write a line: every ingest call, a reject included, but not a run that dies before ingest finishes (trail spec-04); not --check, which returns before materialization (trail spec-08); each for its own kind of run.
At what point the line is written: trail spec-08 places the standalone fail-closed write trail spec-05 keeps out of promote in the CLI ingest handlers, after materialization.
How a reject is recorded: trail spec-04 writes a reject line for every gate reject; trail spec-09 derives that disposition as reject when the patch set's edits are empty.
How the unreviewed reason is bounded: trail spec-03 truncates it to 240 codepoints and lint checks its length; trail spec-06 leaves it unscrubbed because of that bound.

How the GCC memory setup is retired: plan-01 replaces the per-agent GCC sections with one on-demand memkernel rule; plan-05 removes every remaining GCC remnant from both trees; the cleanup completes the replacement.

How a project gets the MCP server registered: plan-03 registers it per project in the uncommitted settings.local.json with its own MEMKERNEL_PROJECT_ID; plan-07 adds that registration step to claude-code sync so existing projects, not just init, get it; it applies plan-03 to one more case.

How existing setups pick up memkernel: setup.sh's --sync path copies the hooks and merges settings for an existing install (plan-06); claude-code sync registers the MCP server for an existing project (plan-07); each for its own target.

Whether the one .cct name holds at home and in the project: spec-01 makes ~/.cct/ the user home so its name matches the project's .cct/; spec-05 rules the project side renamed too, as a separate issue; it extends spec-01's direction to the project.
How the per-project rename is delivered: spec-04 makes the project half its own issue and PR if D5 says yes; spec-05, D5, says yes, after this feature's PR; it settles spec-04's condition.

Whether the plugin ships what its agents and commands refer to: plan-02 ships the six always-on skills as ordinary plugin skills that load on a matching description, said plainly in docs/install.md, rather than leaving them out; plan-04 ships templates/sdd/ and review-decide.sh inside the plugin with rewritten paths, rather than packaging only the self-contained components; each for its own components.
When a memory is withdrawn: spec-01 defines the withdrawn marker; spec-03 decides when a deleted page's memory gets it.
When a memory is withdrawn: spec-04's withdrawal with reason superseded and its late link use spec-01's two markers.
When a memory is withdrawn: spec-05 withdraws a deprecated page's memory with spec-01's marker once the revision is approved.
When a memory is withdrawn: deletion and supersession are two causes, each with its own rule.
When a memory is withdrawn: deletion and deprecation are two causes, each with its own rule.
When a memory is withdrawn: supersession and deprecation are two causes, each with its own rule.
What happens to a renamed page's memory: spec-03 says a rename that kept its page_id is no deletion; the governed spec makes the import supersede it at the new path.
How the import finds a page's previous memory: by page key at another path (governed spec), and only among this wiki's memories (wiki scope).
When a retain is a dedup hit: the content-and-type key holds for memories in general; sourced code dedups per path.
When a retain is a dedup hit: the content-and-type key in general; a wiki memory only for the wiki that owns it.
When a retain is a dedup hit: per path for sourced code; by wiki membership for wiki memories.
How a stale code memory is detected and marked: plan-01 compares content hashes; plan-02 marks the result as a needs_review flag.
What serialises wiki imports: the store-locks spec provides the named wiki-import lock; the wiki-scope spec holds it for every import.
Who writes tags: merge_tags is the one tag writer; the wiki-scope spec writes identity tags through it.
Which operations set identity tags: set_wiki_identity changes only those tags; spec-09 reserves them to it and to the import's retain keyword.
What runs without fcntl: the recall log runs unlocked with one warning, like the store locks it names.
What runs without fcntl: the recall log and the wiki import each run unlocked with one warning, for their own lock.
What runs without fcntl: the wiki import's unlocked run follows the store-locks platform rule and lists the races it leaves.
What the identity tags are: spec-01 defines the terms; spec-02 decides the two tags and membership by them.
When a legacy memory is a candidate: only when no owned candidate exists (spec-04), and it is adopted only on the owner's word (spec-05).
How a 0.6 store is adopted on upgrade: the upgrade run checks the wiki-scope rule, nothing written by default and adopt_legacy adopting without duplicates.
What keys the sync ledger: spec-02 keys it by wiki_id or the path hash; spec-07 migrates it when a manifest is added.
Where memkernel keeps its state: the session spool sits in the same state directory spec-02 creates for the ledger.
How the spool records and drains sessions: the hooks spec writes and drains it; the wiring spec prunes sessions that never ended.
Which injected text is quoted: spec-01 lists the pieces of text; spec-05 lists the blocks where the quoting applies.
Which recalls are logged: spec-02 logs the tool and the hook blocks; spec-01 logs on_post_compact's block only when given a session id.
Which hook blocks are logged: each block that shows memories (spec-03), the post-compact one only with a session id (spec-01).
Which recalls are logged: spec-03 gives the reason spec-02 logs hook blocks, since a session start shows memories without recall.
Which captured records may be candidates: 0.14 replaces 0.12's rule that every captured record stays out; at most 2 owner answers may now be candidates.
What caps bound a capture run: 0.14 keeps 0.12's per-run record cap and adds the owner-answer cap.
Which extractors ship by yield: 0.12 ships one and leaves the extractors with yield to S3; 0.14 names S3's first two.
Filter or collection: session scoping in the MVP and agent or task scope in 0.15 each choose a metadata filter over separate collections.
Who supplies the agent or task id: the caller, never memkernel (spec-06), passed per call or per process (spec-02).
How many chains: spec-01 adopts the eight chains, extended to 12 by D7; spec-07 is D7 and its arithmetic.
Which curator drives the governed arm: the scripted curator is the primary arm (spec-03); the oracle curator is the upper bound (spec-02).
How the 9,000-character budget is shared: the curation debt section and the stored-memory tags each fit inside it by their own rule.
On which wheels the evidence is recorded: released wheels, so 0.7.0 ships first (plan-01); a CI run on a PR wheel is only a signal (plan-05).

cross_pairs.reason: How a failure's class is derived from its raw error output: the probe matches substrings of the exception text, type signals first; the routing classifier maps exit code and output to a cause taxonomy; each for its own system.

Which directory is CCT's user home: the one-harness-home ruling makes it ~/.cct/; the catalog's home, first ~/.code-copilot-team/ through one helper so #411 moves it later, is amended to ${CCT_HOME:-~/.cct} through #411's resolver; the amendment follows the ruling.

How a CCT tool's user home is overridden: the one-harness-home ruling makes CCT_HOME the override for every tool; the catalog's amended home is ${CCT_HOME:-~/.cct}; it applies the one override to the catalog's files.

How the catalog and the user-home move are sequenced: the one-harness-home ruling lets whichever lands first move llms.toml, with the #400 spec amended on record; the catalog's user-home decision carries that amendment, made because #411 landed first; it records the coupling's outcome.

Where in the user's home CCT's registry files live: routing.toml under ~/.code-copilot-team/; the catalog's files there too, amended to ${CCT_HOME:-~/.cct} through one resolver; each for its own files.
Whether a new registry gets its own file beside providers.toml: routing.toml and llms.toml each do, and providers.toml stays the reviewer profile; each for its own registry.

How a CCT TOML registry is parsed: the catalog extracts the line lexer of routing-config.sh, the one parser the routing registry introduced, into a library both registries share; it builds on the routing parser.

How a backend canary is probed and classified: the catalog shares routing-probe.sh's canary primitives and closed tri-state, without its accounting, caps or state runner; it builds on the routing probe engine.

Where an agent tool's memkernel memory instructions live: CCT puts all of them in one on-demand rule its agents reference; memkernel's 0.13 spec picks per tool a SessionStart hook or an always-applied rule (Codex, Cursor, Antigravity); each for its own tools.

How CCT checks a sibling package is usable before running it: memkernel's hook guards check the CLI on PATH and that python3 imports the package; the wiki launcher checks the repo venv's distribution metadata for exactly 0.9.0 and never uses a PATH binary or system interpreter; each for its own package.

Which artifact of a sibling package CCT's setup installs: memkernel, before its publication, editable from a local path, with PyPI named for later; wiki-studio as the exact 0.9.0 wheel with its published SHA-256; each for its own package and its publication state.

Whether the in-repo system a package replaces is removed in the same change: every GCC remnant leaves both adapter trees; both duplicate wiki engines are deleted, with a guard against their return; each for its own replaced system.

Where the user-level configuration lives: the harness plan put it under ~/.code-copilot-team/; the one-harness-home ruling moves the user home to ~/.cct/, replacing that location. Labelled by the owner at the review (2026-11-24): a ruling that only changes where a file lives supersedes the earlier location, the same reading as the existing harness-plan and project-config pair.

How files reach a renamed location: the user home moves only by the explicit cct home migrate, never overwriting; the project configuration by an explicit command only, nothing moved silently; each for its own location.

How long the old location is still read: the user home's fallback runs through 2.1.x and goes in the first 2.2 change; the project configuration's fallback is set with the user-home fallback, so both legacy names go together in 2.2 when both ship in 2.1.0; it builds on the user-home window.
Which command moves files to the new location: cct home migrate is the only mover for the user home; pi-code migrate, beside init and sync, moves the project's files; each for its own files.

Where the committed per-project configuration lives: the harness plan put it in trusted .code-copilot-team/ project files; the one-harness-home ruling names that file and has it renamed in a separate issue, without setting the new location; it builds on the plan's placement.

Where the renamed project configuration lives: the one-harness-home ruling renames the project side in a separate issue, noting that a committed file inside the untracked .cct/ needs a gitignore exception; the project-config spec puts it in .cct.toml at the root, not .cct/config.toml; it is that issue's location ruling.

Whether the renamed project configuration needs a gitignore exception: the one-harness-home ruling leaves the gitignore guidance to the project-side issue; the project-config spec needs none, init keeps .cct/ ignored and doctor warns if .cct.toml is ignored; it gives the deferred guidance.

Which fallback the project-side rename carries: the one-harness-home ruling leaves it to the project-side issue; the project-config spec reads the old location through 2.1.x and removes it in 2.2; it supplies the deferred fallback.

Which manifest rule the project-side rename carries: the one-harness-home ruling notes that pi-code init's manifest records the path and hash and leaves the rule to the project-side issue; the project-config spec puts the manifest at .cct-init.json beside .cct.toml; it supplies the deferred rule.
May an in-repo configuration layer widen policy: Pi's protected-security chain and the routing repository block each answer no, for their own configuration.
May an in-repo configuration layer widen policy: the scrub's tighten-only repo layers and the restriction-only routing block, each for its own setting.
Who supplies an agent's identity: the team controller takes a declared id and memkernel takes the harness's id, each in its own system.

Whether a plugin-only installation works as far as a setup.sh install: the plugin plan ships templates/sdd/ and review-decide.sh inside the plugin so every command does; the wiki-studio adoption claims no automatic installation parity for plugin-only installs, whose guidance names the external prerequisite and refuses without it, a portable plugin tool environment left to a successor; each for its own components.

Whether stored records are scrubbed when written: routing evidence scrubs secrets at the point the record is written; the audit archive gets no scrubber and is held to the curator's review like any wiki page; each for its own records.

Whether a second immediate run is a no-op: routing tick's second run finds nothing due, a byte-level state no-op; audit-flush's second flush finds nothing to flush and exits 0; each for its own command.

How an upstream project's changes may reach what CCT runs: Ponytail's never do, since CCT takes no dependency on it and re-expresses its ideas natively; wiki-studio's only by a CCT commit, since CCT pins the exact wheel rather than a version floor; each for its own upstream.

How an upstream project's changes may reach what CCT runs: Ponytail's do not flow into CCT automatically, its ideas re-expressed under CCT's requirements; wiki-studio's arrive only through a reviewed, atomic CCT pin bump; each for its own upstream.
What an audit-flush commit holds: the flush spec commits only the ingest log by pathspec; CCT's contract test proves a real run committed only the ingest log; the test builds on the flush rule.
Whether a flush right after a flush is a no-op: the flush spec makes it nothing to flush; CCT's contract test proves a second dry-run reported nothing pending; the test builds on the flush rule.
Who verifies the ingest log's proposal-hash recipe: CCT records it verbatim for its deferred cross-referential lint; memkernel reads no ingest log, so it has no consumer; each for its own system.

How a package installed beside wiki-studio settles its mcp extra's MCP 2.x requirement: CCT forbids the extra because Session Analytics targets MCP 1.x; memkernel moves to mcp>=2.3,<3 to co-install with it; each for its own environment.

What happens when wiki-studio is missing or the wrong version: CCT's launcher stops and names the setup command; memkernel's auto mode uses its direct writer when wiki-studio is absent and refuses when it is broken or too old; each in its own system.

Whether a wiki moves to wiki-studio's governed mode: CCT runs no init and keeps its wiki manifest-less; memkernel's governed setting refuses a legacy wiki and names wiki-studio init, while auto keeps today's path; each for its own deployment.

Which wiki-studio release CI installs: CCT's CI installs the exact pinned wheel production runs; memkernel's informational workflow installs the newest release in range so an upstream change shows; each for its own purpose.
